submodelElements.value: The most probable root cause is a Dual Fault Scenario: (1) a Total Failure of the p_FMU Pressure Sensor AND (2) a concurrent, separate instance of Main Fuel Pump Over-performance. Reasoning: The data clearly shows two distinct problems that are not physically dependent on each other. The first is the undeniable dropout of the p_FMU sensor, which is an isolated electrical or component failure. The second is a classic fuel over-delivery signature, where the pump is producing too much flow, and the rest of the system is reacting accordingly (high bypass flow, high engine flow). Neither of these faults can cause the other. A pump performing at +12% would not cause an adjacent pressure sensor to read -99%. Likewise, a failed pressure sensor would not cause the physical pump to deliver more fuel. Therefore, the only logical conclusion is that the system has suffered two simultaneous, independent failures.

value.value: Dual Fault: Sensor Dropout & Pump Over-performance

This is the only hypothesis that explains all symptoms. There are two independent failures: 1) The p_FMU sensor has failed, causing the dropout. 2) The Main Fuel Pump is significantly over-performing (+12.2%), causing the high readings on Flow_Pump, Flow_Bypass, and Flow_Engine. These two faults are happening concurrently.

This explains the critical -99.4% reading. However, a sensor-only fault cannot explain the separate, physically consistent pattern of over-performance seen in Flow_Pump, Flow_Bypass, and the engine flows.
This explains the high flow readings across the board. However, it does not explain why the p_FMU pressure sensor, specifically, drops to zero while other pressure sensors remain healthy.

A massive leak at the FMU could theoretically cause the local pressure (p_FMU) to drop to zero. However, this contradicts all other data: a leak would cause flow and pressure to decrease downstream, but here Flow_Engine is high, and Flow_Pump is also high.

It is extremely unlikely that the p_FMU sensor would fail (dropout) at the same time as the Flow_Pump and Flow_Bypass sensors all fail with a positive offset in a way that perfectly mimics a real physical over-performance scenario. The dual physical/sensor fault is far more plausible
